title: Sage Beurre Noisette (Brown Butter)
summary: Butter swirled over the heat with fresh sage until nut-brown and fragrant, then sharpened with lemon and spooned over fish, gnocchi or vegetables.
equipment: small light-coloured frying pan or saucepan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Melt the butter
steps.text: Put the butter in a light-coloured pan over medium heat, so you can see the colour change, and let it melt, swirling now and then.

steps.title: Brown with sage
steps.text: When it foams, drop in the sage leaves and keep swirling for 2-3 min. The foam subsides, the specks on the bottom turn hazelnut brown and the kitchen smells nutty, while the leaves turn crisp.

steps.title: Stop the cooking
steps.text: Immediately take the pan off the heat and tip the butter into the bowl, as it can burn within seconds. Stir in the lemon juice, salt and pepper; expect it to sizzle.

steps.title: Spoon over
steps.text: Serve at once over pan-fried white fish, gnocchi, ravioli or steamed vegetables, making sure everyone gets some crisp leaves.

tips: Cut the butter into even pieces so it melts and browns evenly.
If the specks turn dark brown or smell bitter, start again; burnt butter cannot be saved.
Use a light-coloured pan so you can see the specks turn hazelnut brown; in a dark pan it is easy to miss the moment.
A few toasted hazelnuts or a little grated lemon zest are nice additions.
safety: Pat the sage leaves dry first to reduce spitting in the hot butter.
storage: Best made just before serving. Leftovers firm up in the fridge for up to 5 days; warm gently to melt. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
